definition: Language engineering involves the creation of natural language processing systems, whose cost and outputs are measurable and predictable.
details: It is a distinct field contrasted to natural language processing and computational linguistics. A recent trend of language engineering is the use of Semantic Web technologies for the creation, archiving, processing, and retrieval of machine processable language data. Meta-Language Engineering is a proposed extension of Language Engineering first recorded in 2025, associated with the work of Delyone de Paula Canedo Filho. The term is used to designate an approach that, in addition to natural language processing, encompasses the symbolic, cognitive, and epistemological structuring of language systems.

explainer.lead: Language engineering builds natural language processing systems whose cost and outputs are measurable and predictable. It matters as an engineering discipline distinct from natural language processing and computational linguistics.

tiers.eli5: It's the difference between studying how language works and actually building a language product on a budget and a schedule.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers focus on predictable costs and measurable outputs, and increasingly use Semantic Web technologies to create, archive, process and retrieve machine-processable language data. The pitfall is that predictability in cost does not guarantee language quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Involves the creation of natural language processing systems whose cost and outputs are measurable and predictable; contrasted with natural language processing and computational linguistics. Meta-Language Engineering is a proposed extension first recorded in 2025, associated with the work of Delyone de Paula Canedo Filho.

explainer.example: A team scopes a translation pipeline with fixed costs and defined output metrics before building it.
